posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
What is the maximum amount of ‘things’ that Omnitron-X can do in one turn?
‘Things’ include dealing damage, playing cards, healing others, drawing cards, and using powers.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Start Phase - Destroy Slip Through Time left over from previous turn. Activate first EDU to play Tech Advancement, searching for a missing component and putting it into play, then drawing a card. Activate second EDU and play Tech Advancement again, searching for the last remaining component, putting it into play, and drawing a card. Activate all other components - two each of Plasma Cannon, Gaussian Coil thingy, and Innervation Ray.

Play Phase - Play Reset, shuffle trash into deck, draw a card, play second copy of Reset, repeat, play third copy of Reset...I think that's it for Resets (repeat again if he actually has four). Off the last Reset, play Slip Through Time.

Power Phase - Timeshift himself, bringing out...Tech Advancement again, I suppose, to put out a plating and draw another card.

Draw Phase - Draw a card.

End Phase - Activate Slip Through Time, playing anything which has a power, then use that power - either punch two things (or the same thing twice) with Rocket Punch, nuke an environment card and deal some damage with Bio-Engineering Beam, or nuke All Of The Things with Defensive Blast.

I think that's it. I probably missed a really obvious way to do a bunch more stuff, though :P.

posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
Eight components fire at the start of his turn (and if you're fighting against someone who can hit you on your turn, then Reactive Plating gives you an extra damage instance or two here, plus with an Elemental Exochassis you can aim your Focused Plasma Cannons at yourself in order to deal extra instances of damage), and you can use the card plays from the EDUs to play Reset, Reset, Reset, Technological Advancement (twice), play Reset, Reset, Reset, Slip Through Time, Timeshift self to put another Reset into play, then play Reset, Reset, Slip Through Time, draw a card, play Reset, play Reset, play Reset, play Reset, play the two Technological Advancements again and use a pair of powers. So scoring one point for each card played or put into play, each card drawn, each power used, each instance of (non-power) damage dealt and each heal, I score 49 (assuming no enemy retaliation damage). Did I miss anything?

EDIT: Ninja'd, but I played seven more Resets than Ameena, so I think I win :D I did forget to blow the Slip Through Times at the start of the turn if that counts though, which would be possible...

posts.name: grysqrl
posts.cooked:
If external sources can be considered (and the question doesn't prohibit it):

  • Embolden on Omni-X could give him another power use and another damage dealt (if one of his last Technological Advancements is used to switch to Temporal Shielding).
  • Time Flies would grant an extra card play and draw.
  • Pillars of Hercules plays a villain card (which could create opportunities to do reaction damage) and grants an extra card play, power use, and card draw.

There are probably some more, but that's what I remembered off the top of my head.

 

Also, no one has brought up that these things only have to be done in one turn - it doesn't say it has to be Omni-X's turn. There may be some chain from Argent Adept that would give him more actions.

 

Edit:

Timeshifting Argent Adept instead of Omni-X could also increase the number of actions.

posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked: For the sake of argument, let's restrict the number to actions only on Omnitron-X's turn with no interference from outside heroes (no Embolden or Argent Adept shenanigans).

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
If your deck and trash are empty, you could play three Resets off the first EDU, then play some other card, let the stack clear, move on to your second EDU, and play the fourth Reset, reshuffling all three Resets into a three-card deck from which you draw and play another Reset three times, then draw the last Reset and let the stack clear again.  Then you can do this again during your play phase, then again during Slip through Time.  (It might also work to put a Reset into play with Timeshift, but I'm less sure how the numbers work out that way.)  So that's 12 (or more) Resets possible in one turn.

That's not exactly the question, but I thought it was cool.  Now if only there was some other hero who had an ability like "Whenever another hero plays a card, this hero regains 1 HP".  That way, you could actually be accomplishing something by standing there with your face-light blinking insistently for twelve solid minutes.  (I suppose if you were very brave, you might do this while fighting Apostate with the Tome of the Unknowable in play, in order to forcibly burn through his deck.)
